::: {.callout-warning}
**Read this page before pointing Claude Code at any project containing
IRB-protected, restricted-access, or otherwise confidential data.** When
in doubt, default to "no" and ask your IRB.
:::

::: {.callout-note}

:::

## What to never send

- **IRB-protected human-subjects data** (interviews, identifiable surveys,
  health data) unless your IRB protocol explicitly permits cloud LLM
  processing — most don't.
- **FERPA-covered student records.**
- **Restricted-access administrative data** (Census, IRS, state
  longitudinal data systems, etc.) — almost universally prohibited from
  any cloud transmission. RDC/FSRDC environments forbid it outright.
- **Confidential firm or proprietary data** under NDA.
- **Refereed manuscripts** without checking journal policy.

## What is generally safe

- Public datasets (IPUMS, Compustat extracts you'd freely share, BLS
  microdata releases, etc.).
- Your own simulated data.
- Code that doesn't reveal the underlying observations.
- Paper drafts on your own work (with co-author awareness).

## Pragmatic workarounds

When you have a restricted dataset and want help with the *code*:

1. **Synthesize a fake version.** Have Claude generate fake data with
   the same schema and let it work on that.
2. **Point it at code only, never data.** Most "clean this `.do` file"
   work doesn't need the actual data; it needs the script.
3. **Run sensitive jobs on the secure environment** with no cloud LLM
   involved, then bring back outputs you're allowed to share.
4. **Use Claude Code only for non-restricted side projects** until you've
   talked to your IRB about an explicit policy.

## Institutional questions to resolve

- Does your university have a policy on LLM use with research data?
- Does your IRB have boilerplate language for cloud LLM processing?
- Do data agreements (DUAs) you've signed permit transmission to
  third-party services?
